text:
Elias Lindholm is giving Boston far more than it got from him last season, and the headlines have followed. He has 17 points in 19 games, a five-game point streak, and by our wins added he ranks 20th among 522 skaters, with his goals adding about three quarters of a win more than the chances behind them.

Now the caution. Boston has scored 8.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, he is shooting 20% against a range that tops out near 17%, and his 3.14 points per 60 sits above anything we would expect from him (our middle estimate is 2.46). Last season Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, with chances against piling up when he played.

What is different this year is real, too: the Bruins are getting 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, 5.4 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 23% of his setups come across the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side. The shooting is the part most likely to cool. Whether that chance share holds tells you which Lindholm Boston really has.
